This is a complete-inventory absence: emit S2 candidate for NL-CONTRACT-REF-009 binding WaterState and MethaneState exact refs. The UnspecifiedInitial leaf is a compiler-owned synthetic placeholder with LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING; per protocol this supports the initial_entry defect for PumpControl's owner-local edge (already captured by NL3-INITENTRY-1) but must not itself become a separate deadlock_freedom issue since it is not an author-specified operating state. decisions.reason: NL3 requires PumpControl's first transition to reach PumpState, but the closed FCSTM gives PumpControl its own default initial edge (transition:line:27) into a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf with zero outgoing transitions (state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:26), while the only edge that actually reaches PumpState (transition:line:13) is owned by the nested Region1 scope that PumpControl's own initial edge never enters. The supplied dossier provides no exact source_refs, element_refs, or model facts from which to establish or refute the root->PumpControl entry claim, so the genuinely undecidable state is preserved. The only competent alternative is that a future exact binding would resolve the check either way, which cannot be adjudicated now.
decisions.strongest_defeater: A later exact owner/carrier binding could resolve this frontier check to a concrete model identity, at which point either the root->PumpControl edge would be confirmed present (satisfying the contract) or confirmed absent/malformed (violating it); absent that binding, no identity was inferred from names, display text, or an incomplete ref set.
decisions.violated_obligation: The system's root scope must have an initial pseudostate edge entering PumpControl.

decisions.basis: dossier-prompt-projection.v4: binding over state:PumpControl:line:8, state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:26, transition:line:27, state:PumpState:line:10, transition:line:13; fcstm_model text and inspection_equivalent_facts transitions; predicate plan unsupported (null); backend receipt unsupported/unknown.
decisions.reason: The fcstm_model text explicitly shows '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;' inside the PumpControl block (transition:line:27) and '[*] -> PumpState;' inside the nested Region1 block (transition:line:13), with UnspecifiedInitial marked as a compiler-owned synthetic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING state having no path to PumpState/Region1. This establishes that PumpControl's owner-local initial edge never reaches PumpState. The candidate itself raises but does not accept the rebuttal that Region1's nested edge could discharge the obligation; per protocol a nested/differently-owned edge cannot satisfy an outer composite's exact owner-scoped entry obligation when the outer composite's own edge demonstrably bypasses that region, but this remains a genuinely competent alternative reading of composite delegation that is not conclusively excluded by the supplied facts alone, so it survives as an undercutting defeater.
decisions.strongest_defeater: Region1's own [*]->PumpState edge (transition:line:13) discharges the substate-entry intent since PumpState is reached whenever Region1 is entered, treating Region1's default entry as functionally equivalent to PumpControl's required entry into PumpState.
decisions.violated_obligation: PumpControl (owner scope) must have its initial pseudostate edge enter PumpState as required by NL3.

decisions.basis: dossier-prompt-projection.v4: binding over state:PumpControl:line:8, state:Region1:line:9, state:Region2:line:19; source llms_emp_feedback_final_0043.puml lines 4,5,13; predicate plan unsupported (null); backend receipt unsupported/unknown.
decisions.reason: NL2 requires three main substates directly under PumpControl. The complete source inventory establishes that PumpControl's exact direct members are Region1 (state:Region1:line:9) and Region2 (state:Region2:line:19) -- only 2 members under the explicit_named_members reading, not 3. This is a complete finite source/model inventory establishing a cardinality shortfall for the exactly bound owner (PumpControl) and member domain. The dossier itself identifies a competent alternative scope/member reading (direct_child_states, i.e., counting PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState directly rather than via the Region1/Region2 containment layer) that is compatible with the same underlying facts and not excluded by the supplied dossier, so it survives as an undercutting defeater per the two-competent-readings protocol.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The three named substates (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) could alternatively be read as the direct child states owned by PumpControl (direct_child_states reading) rather than counted against the explicit_named_members domain that instead finds only Region1 and Region2 as PumpControl's direct source members.
decisions.violated_obligation: Within PumpControl composite membership, PumpControl must realize 3 main substates (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) under the explicit named-member reading.

result.reason: Each prior decision was rejected only because it lacked a non-null strongest_defeater while asserting a typed (non-none) defeater kind/disposition. This correction preserves the same grounding and defeater_kind/disposition determinations already justified by the supplied facts, but supplies the required strongest_defeater text (drawn from each dossier's own strongest_rebuttal/candidate reasoning) so the defeater is fully typed and auditable.

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions rows for transition:line:27 (scope=PumpControl, target=UnspecifiedInitial) and transition:line:13 (scope=Region1, target=PumpState); verify_facts proved rows initial-entry:transition:line:27 and initial-entry:transition:line:13 confirm both edges exist but at different scopes; NL-CONTRACT-NL3-INITENTRY-1 owner hint=PumpControl, target=PumpState.
issues.expected: PumpControl (the exact owner named by the NL2/NL3 narrative that directly contains the three named substates) must have an initial pseudostate edge whose target is PumpState.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM's PumpControl-owned initial edge (transition:line:27, scope=PumpControl) targets a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf state with no outgoing transitions (transition:line:26/state:UnspecifiedInitial), not PumpState. The only initial edge reaching PumpState (transition:line:13) is owned by the nested Region1 composite, a scope the NL narrative never introduces; PumpControl's own default-entry initial edge never reaches PumpState.
issues.reason: NL2 and NL3 together describe PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState as the three main substates directly narrated under PumpControl, and NL3 requires PumpControl's first transition to reach PumpState. The closed FCSTM instead gives PumpControl its own default entry into a compiler-synthesized UnspecifiedInitial leaf that has zero outgoing transitions, while the only edge reaching PumpState is owned by an author-unintroduced nested Region1 scope. This is an owner-scope initial-entry defect distinct from the satisfied root->PumpControl contract.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue that Region1's [*]->PumpState edge together with PumpControl's structural containment of Region1 transitively realizes 'PumpControl enters PumpState first'. However, per the owner-scope discipline, an initial edge owned by a nested region cannot satisfy an entry contract owned by the outer composite when the outer composite's own default initial edge exists and demonstrably targets a different, non-equivalent leaf (UnspecifiedInitial) instead of delegating to Region1.
issues.title: PumpControl lacks an owner-local default entry into PumpState; its actual default entry targets a synthetic dead-end state

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions (tr_0003..tr_0006) and inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions (lines 14-17) show only PumpState<->WaterState and PumpState<->MethaneState edges; no WaterState->MethaneState edge exists in either author-source or closed-model inventories.
issues.expected: A transition from WaterState to MethaneState must exist within the PumpControl/Region1 scope, per the sequential narrative in NL4-NL5 (PumpState -> WaterState -> MethaneState).
issues.observed: The complete closed transition inventory contains exactly one outgoing edge from WaterState: WaterState -> PumpState (transition:line:16, triggered by _Water_Flow_Completed). No WaterState -> MethaneState edge exists anywhere in the inventory (inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions, 10 total rows) or in the exact source inventory (tr_0005: WaterState -> PumpState only).
issues.reason: NL5 explicitly requires a transition from WaterState to MethaneState as a distinct exact edge (transition_endpoints, violation_direction=wrong_target). The complete exact_source_inventory.transitions and inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions lists contain no such edge; WaterState's sole outgoing edge (tr_0005/transition:line:16) targets PumpState instead. This is a complete-inventory absence, so the absent edge is the candidate evidence and the exact existing endpoint state refs are bound.
issues.requirement_quote: Similarly, the system can transition to the MethaneState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The exact author-source and closed-model transitions instead form a hub-and-spoke pattern around PumpState (PumpState<->WaterState, PumpState<->MethaneState), which may be the intended semantic model even though NL5's literal sequential phrasing ("the system can transition to the MethaneState substate" following WaterState narrative) reads as WaterState->MethaneState; the actual author transitions never establish this edge from WaterState, only from PumpState.
issues.title: No WaterState->MethaneState transition exists in the closed model; WaterState's only outgoing edge targets PumpState

issues.basis: fcstm_model text: '[*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;' inside PumpControl block, and '[*] -> PumpState;' inside the nested Region1 block; inspection_equivalent_facts transitions transition:line:27 (scope=PumpControl, source=[*], target=UnspecifiedInitial) versus transition:line:13 (scope=Region1, source=[*], target=PumpState); working_contract elements marking UnspecifiedInitial as compiler-owned synthetic_state.
issues.expected: PumpControl (the owner scope) must have its initial pseudostate edge enter PumpState as required by NL3.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM's PumpControl-owned initial edge (transition:line:27, scope=PumpControl) targets UnspecifiedInitial, a compiler-owned synthetic leaf with LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and no path to PumpState/Region1. The authored Region1-local initial edge ([*]->PumpState, transition:line:13/tr_0002) exists but is owned by the nested Region1 scope, not by PumpControl directly, and Region1 itself is never entered because PumpControl's own initial edge bypasses it entirely.
issues.reason: Per the strict owner-scoped initial_entry rule, PumpControl is the exact owner named in this contract's binding hints, and its own initial edge must reach PumpState (or the scope containing it) for the contract to be satisfied. The closed FCSTM diverts PumpControl's initial edge to a synthetic dead leaf, so from PumpControl's perspective PumpState is never entered by default; this is an exact missing owner-local entry, not merely an entry into a different but valid substate.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue Region1's own [*]->PumpState edge (transition:line:13) discharges the substate-entry intent since PumpState is reached whenever Region1 is entered; however PumpControl's actual owner-local edge never enters Region1 at all, so this nested edge can never fire, and per protocol a nested/differently-owned edge cannot satisfy the contract's exact owner-scoped obligation.
issues.title: PumpControl's owner-local initial edge targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial instead of PumpState

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL (lines 9,10,11,12); verify_facts.checks.non_proved reachability rows for state:Region1:line:9, state:PumpState:line:10, state:WaterState:line:11, state:MethaneState:line:12; reachable_state_refs in inspection_equivalent_facts omits all four.
issues.expected: The Region1 operating scope, required to host the pump/water/methane substates entered per NL2-NL5, must be reachable from the machine's top-level initial entry (root -> PumpControl -> Region1).
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts both mark Region1, PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState as reachable_from_initial=false / refuted, because PumpControl's actual initial edge routes to the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf instead of into Region1.
issues.reason: NL2 through NL5 establish PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState as required operating substates that the system must actually enter and transition among; this is impossible unless the enclosing Region1 region is reachable from root. Deterministic finite reachability results close this as refuted for the entire subtree, which is a distinct global-topology defect from the narrower owner-local initial_entry contract on PumpControl.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Region1's own local initial edge ([*]->PumpState) is present and well-formed in isolation, so one could argue the sub-structure itself is correctly authored and only the outer owner-entry is defective; however the global reachability property is independently violated regardless of local well-formedness, since no execution path from the machine root can ever enter Region1.
issues.title: Region1 (housing PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState) is unreachable from the top-level initial entry

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers rows for the four named events (declared_ref/consumer_transition_refs non-empty, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE entries for these four events; verify_facts.checks.non_proved event_consumer rows for the same four events.
issues.expected: The flow-detection/completion event transitions between PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState (required by NL2-NL5 to drive substate switching) must have at least one operationally reachable consumer from the top-level initial entry.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers lists non-empty consumer_transition_refs for all four events (_Water_Flow_Detected, _Methane_Flow_Detected, _Water_Flow_Completed, _Methane_Flow_Completed) but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty for every one, and diagnostics explicitly flag EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for each; verify_facts independently refutes each event-consumer check.
issues.reason: NL2 through NL5 require the pump substates to respond to water/methane flow conditions by transitioning; this is an operational event-response obligation distinct from mere declaration. The deterministic event-consumer facts show declaration-only coverage with zero reachable consumers, which directly violates the reachable-consumer-coverage property for this exact scope.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the PumpControl state, there are three main substates: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The events are declared and their consuming transitions exist structurally in the model (tr_0003-tr_0006 equivalents), so one could argue declaration-level coverage is satisfied and unreachability is purely a consequence of the already-identified initial_entry defect rather than an independent event-coverage problem; however operational coverage is a distinct property from declaration, and this obligation is about actual runtime responsiveness to flow events, which currently cannot occur under any execution.
issues.title: Water/Methane flow events have declared consumers but zero reachable consumer transitions

This makes Region1, PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState, Region2, Idle, and Active all unreachable_from_initial per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts, and every declared event consumer for the six events is unreachable. This behaviorally defeats NL3's PumpControl->PumpState initial-entry contract, and licenses one derived reachability contract for the Region1 scope with no path from its owner PumpControl. The UnspecifiedInitial leaf is a compiler-owned synthetic placeholder with LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING; per protocol this supports the initial_entry defect for PumpControl's owner-local edge (already captured by NL3-INITENTRY-1) but must not itself become a separate deadlock_freedom issue since it is not an author-specified operating state. I therefore emit: (1) NL3-INITENTRY-1 as violated because PumpControl's actual initial edge targets UnspecifiedInitial, not PumpState; (2) NL4-ENDPOINT-1 and NL5-ENDPOINT-1 remain satisfied as literal edges exist in the FCSTM (transition:line:14, transition:line:15) - omitted since endpoint existence is distinct from reachability; (3) I derive one additional reachability contract for the Region1 operating scope since it is completely unreachable from root, distinct from the owner-local initial_entry defect; (4) event_consumer_coverage derived contract for the four Region1-relevant events since NL3/NL4/NL5 require these substates to be operationally entered and their event-driven transitions consumed, but facts show zero reachable consumers.
